name: Hermanus Central and the Cliff Path
tagline: The town centre above the bay, where the whales come
description: The compact centre on the cliff above Walker Bay, with the old harbour, the shops and restaurants around Market Square, and the cliff path running along the edge in both directions. Between June and November the southern right whales calve close enough to watch from the benches.
bestFor: Anyone who wants the cliff path, the shops and the whales all on foot
pros: The cliff path and the whale viewing directly there
All shops, restaurants and services close by
Genuinely walkable, unusual for a South African town
cons: The highest rents in town, higher again in whale season
Very busy in the December holidays and the whale festival

name: Voelklip and Eastcliff
tagline: The eastern residential slopes, with Grotto Beach below
description: The residential districts east of the centre climbing the slope towards the mountain, with Grotto Beach, a long blue-flag stretch of sand, at the bottom. It is quiet, well kept and popular with retirees and holiday-home owners, about ten minutes from the centre.
bestFor: Longer stays wanting a quiet house near the long beach
pros: Grotto Beach and its blue-flag sand below
cons: Ten minutes into the centre, usually by car
High rents in the summer holidays

name: Fernkloof and Northcliff
tagline: Up against the nature reserve, fynbos at the door
description: The upper streets on the northern side of town, running into the Fernkloof Nature Reserve, which protects a substantial area of fynbos with a well-marked trail network and several hundred plant species. Houses here look down over the bay with the mountain immediately behind.
bestFor: Stays where a fynbos walk before work matters more than a beach
pros: Fernkloof reserve and its trails at the top of the street
cons: Steep, and a car is needed
Ten to fifteen minutes to the shops
Wildfire risk in dry, windy conditions

name: Hemel-en-Aarde Valley
tagline: The wine valley behind the town, pinot noir and chardonnay
description: The valley running inland from Hermanus, one of South Africa's best cool-climate wine regions, with estates producing pinot noir and chardonnay and several of them running restaurants. Accommodation is guest cottages and farm stays among the vines, ten minutes from town.
bestFor: Stays that want the vineyards and the estate restaurants rather than the sea
pros: Some of South Africa's best cool-climate wine estates
Estate restaurants and tastings within minutes
cons: Ten to fifteen minutes into town

name: Sandbaai and Onrus
tagline: The settlements west along the coast, better value
description: The coastal villages running west from Hermanus towards Vermont, with a swimming lagoon at Onrus, a small beach and a more ordinary residential character. Rents here are noticeably below Hermanus proper and the drive into town takes about ten minutes.
bestFor: Longer stays wanting the same coast at a lower rent
pros: Onrus lagoon and a sheltered swimming beach
cons: Ten to fifteen minutes into Hermanus
Less to look at than the cliff path
